title: Okinawa Celebrates Restoration of Shuri Castle
paragraphs: Officials and residents in Okinawa celebrated the restoration of Shuri Castle's main hall on November 22, seven years after it was destroyed in a fire.
The building, famous for its deep red color and dragon decorations, is an important symbol of Okinawa's cultural heritage.

The fire broke out on October 31, 2019 during a festival at the castle complex in Naha, Okinawa's capital. Firefighters struggled for nearly 12 hours to contain the blaze as it spread in strong winds. The fire destroyed the main hall, two halls next to it and four nearby structures, while two other structures were heavily damaged.
Investigators could not determine the cause but considered an electrical fault the likeliest explanation.
"The fire was a tremendous shock to the Okinawan people," Okinawa Governor Genta Koja said at the restoration ceremony.
Shuri Castle dates back to the Ryukyu Kingdom, which ruled Okinawa for about 450 years until Japan took control in 1879.
The castle also represents Okinawa's recovery from World War II. It was destroyed during the Battle of Okinawa in 1945, which killed about 200,000 people, including many civilians.
The castle was largely rebuilt in 1992, but work on some sections was still underway when the 2019 fire occurred.

For the latest restoration, experts used historical documents and new research to make the main hall more closely resemble the original building. They even recreated its distinctive deep red color using a pigment made partly from iron bacteria found in northern Okinawa.
The main hall reopened to the public on November 23, while restoration of other buildings will continue in stages. Experts say completing the entire castle could take more than a decade.
Shuri Castle is a major tourist attraction, and its restoration is expected to boost Okinawa's economy.
Koja, who took office in September, has promised to double the island's per capita income and tourism revenue within a decade and make it more attractive to young people.
